## Verifying a build

A local Distribution build is only ever checked, never launched: it loads
Sparkle, which library validation refuses in an ad-hoc signed hardened app
(spec §11 PUB-7). Debug and Release link with `-dead_strip_dylibs`, so they
never load it.

The app is verified by driving the built binary over MCP and comparing what
it renders — not by reading code. Launch your own instance on your own socket
and only ever kill that one (`pgrep -f "MacOS/Frame Job"` lists them, Debug
and Release alike; the products folder tells them apart; another session may
have one running):

```sh
make app-debug
python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch   # prints folder, socket, log, pid
```

Each later command names the printed folder literally
(`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")`, `python3 tools/proof/phaseN_proof.py
<dir>/agent.sock`, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`), because a shell
variable does not survive from one agent command to the next; stop it by the
pid the launcher prints.

The log line `Frame Job agent socket listening at <dir>/agent.sock` says it is
up (`not bound: <reason>` says why not). Drive it with `tools/proof/mcp.py`'s
`mcp.MCP("<dir>/agent.sock")` (streamable HTTP over the Unix socket), or with
the bundled stdio helper `framejob-mcp` with `RC_AGENT_SOCKET` set to the same
path: one tool per §6 op, each taking the `scope`
envelope key, plus the app-state tools — `open_project`, `new_project`,
`save_project`, `close_project`, `get_project`, `import_media`,
`import_captions`, `export_captions`, `transcribe`, `consolidate_media`, `detect_silence`,
`detect_fillers`, `transcribe_for_fillers`, `get_transcript`, `normalize_clip`, `set_playhead`, `set_range`, `set_selection`, `set_scope`,
`undo`, `redo`, `render_frame`, `export`, `export_status`, `cancel_export`,
`record_screen`, `write_graphic`,
`get_graphic`, `graphic_reference`, `render_graphic`, `import_graphic_font`,
`import_graphic_asset`, `delete_graphic`, `rename_graphic`,
`restore_graphic`, `list_graphics`, `insert_graphic`, `export_graphic` and `import_graphic`. A Debug or Release build also has the dev tools
(`snapshot_ui`, `perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`;
"Seeing the chrome" below; `play_preview`, which plays a window's preview
for a while and answers the frames composed (#127, spec §11 G-36);
`graphic_memory`, which answers the graphic rasters' memory budget, what is
held and kept, and simulates memory pressure (G-37); and
`assistant_send` / `assistant_answer`, which
drive a window's assistant turn against a stand-in server, with the dev-only
launch default `-RCDevAssistantSend <text> -RCDevAssistantReport <path>` for
a turn in a launch without the server; and `-RCDevSyncHold <s>`, which holds
Synchronize Audio's background analysis so a proof can act during it; and
`-RCDevRampRenderHold <s>`, which holds each speed-ramp audio render so a
proof can act while it is pending; and `-RCDevWebMFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`,
which puts a fault in an `av1_webm` export's audio pump or video sink so a
proof can time the stop, spec §11 CX-15 (6); and
`-RCDevGraphicImportAccept YES`, with which the Import Graphic sheet presses
its own Import so a proof can see a package land (spec §11 G-47); and
`-RCDevExportFault audio@N|video@N|audio-hold@N`, the same for an
`ExportWriter` export's pumps, spec §11 #378), which
Distribution does not. `rc_op_names`
and the catalog are the authority for the counts; the parity check compares
them at startup. `render_frame` writes a PNG and returns its path; `export`
puts the job on the Export Queue and answers an `export_id` at once, and
`export_status` answers it until `done` (`mcp.py`'s `export_with` waits; spec
§11 #326).

A proof picks its app through `tools/proof/proof_app.py`: `RC_PROOF_APP` is
`debug` (the default), `release` or a `.app` path. `mcp.launch`, `mcp.MCP` and
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch` refuse a tree's built app when any
input is newer than its last complete build (its
`_CodeSignature/CodeResources`), or an instance started before an input
changed, naming the file, its time and the `make` target.

Release-only proofs pass `release_only=` (`git grep release_only= tools/proof`);
recording_proof's socket instance is started with
`python3 tools/proof/proof_app.py launch --app release`.

**Before trusting any MCP proof, `grep "Frame Job: " <dir>/framejob.log`
must print nothing** — that prefix is the startup parity check complaining.
On a Debug build the same complaint is an `assertionFailure` that traps first
(`AgentServer.prepareCatalog`), so `make app-debug` fails at Write Agent
Catalog with `Fatal error: …` instead of logging the line.

A proof's instance shares its bundle's defaults domain (the owner's
`com.kgalligan.FrameJob` for a Release build, `com.kgalligan.FrameJob.debug`
for a Debug build, spec §11 V-5): no
environment moves `UserDefaults` (#238). Never perform a persisting menu item
(View ▸ Snapping, Safe Areas, Hide Inspector, Timeline Track Height, Preview
Quality) on either build: `mcp.py` ends the script with status 3 and
`DEFAULTS MOVED` last on stderr when its session moved a key and no other
Frame Job shares the domain, and only prints the line when one does;
`defaults_proof.py` is its proof. The guard reads the domain with
`CFFIXED_USER_HOME` taken out of `defaults`' environment
(`proof_defaults.read_env`), so a proof run under a scratch home that does
not exist yet, or is removed before the script ends, is compared with
itself: `defaults export` answers no key under a variable naming an absent
folder.

**`tools/proof/` holds the scripts that do this** — an MCP script per phase
over a dependency-free client (`mcp.py`), and beside most of them an
offscreen-chrome script or a probe. Every claim in them is a placement read
back through `get_project`, a BYTE comparison of two PNGs, or a
sample-for-sample comparison of two exports decoded to PCM (which needs
`ffmpeg` at proof time). Its README says how to make the test media, run
one, and which scores are known host-state skips (a locked console, a
Bluetooth output). Add the next phase's proof there rather than writing a
throwaway. An instance DEADLOCKS somewhere past forty documents open at once:
a proof that closes what it opens (`close_project`) can share an instance, and
one that does not relaunches between proof sessions.

Spec §10's per-step verifications are the acceptance tests. What no script
can answer — step 4's "the clip plays with audio", step 5's 60 fps, and the
rest — is a row in `docs/manual-checks.md`, which the owner runs.

## Verification

- **In the loop:** a targeted test (`cd core && cargo test --release --test
  <file> <filter>`), `make lint` after Rust edits, `make typecheck` after Swift
  edits, `make app-debug` before driving the app, and the phase's own rows
  (`--only` where the proof has it) against Debug.
- **Once, when the code is complete:** `make gate`, in the foreground, under
  the 600 s tool cap (`make gate GATE_ARGS=--force` only when a stamp itself is
  in doubt). It stops at the first failure and skips a step whose inputs and
  tools are byte-identical to its last pass, so after a fix it re-runs only
  what the fix can change. Never run one of its steps by hand to stand in for
  it, never re-run an unchanged step, and never run anything twice with no
  edit between.
- **The proof a phase records** runs whole once, on the final instrument,
  against Release (`RC_PROOF_APP=release` after the gate's `make app`), with
  any `release_only` proof the change touches. This is a rule: nothing checks
  which build a recorded run drove.
- **A proof that fails only on Debug** is pinned `release_only="<reason>"` in
  the change that finds it (spec §11 V-4); an assert trap on Debug is a defect
  to fix, never a pin.
- **Mutants** target the decisions the phase adds: about one per new branch,
  threshold, refusal or ordering, usually 3–8; more than 10 only with a reason
  written in the spec. The full set runs once, at the end, on the final
  instrument.
- **A fix pass** re-runs only the rows whose instrument code it changed and
  the mutants whose anchor lines it touched, then `make gate`.
- **Background** only for a command that cannot fit 600 s, waited on once with
  a bound; never a poll loop.

## Seeing the chrome

`screencapture` needs a Screen Recording grant the agent's terminal may or
may not have (it varies by host and session), and without it `screencapture`
silently writes a black PNG. Assume neither: a proof that needs the grant
probes for it and skips its granted tier by name, and a capture is never
trusted until it is checked non-black. The way to LOOK at the chrome is
**`tools/proof/harness/`**: it compiles every file in `app/Sources` except
`main.swift` with a `main.swift` of its own, links the staticlib, opens a
`.framejob` package, puts an `EditorViewController` in an `NSWindow` and
`cacheDisplay`s it into a PNG at the display's backing scale — the same paint
path the window uses, no TCC grant, either appearance, captured on SETTLE.
The preview well comes out as the canvas background (an `AVPlayerLayer` or
Metal layer does not draw into `cacheDisplay`), so nothing about the PICTURE
is ever claimed offscreen; pixel claims go over MCP. `tools/proof/README.md`'s
"offscreen harness" section has the build line, the argument list and the
pinned `UserDefaults`.

To look at the LIVE app, a Debug or Release build (`make app-debug`,
`make app`; never Distribution) has dev tools over MCP (road map 11, spec §11 V-1).
`snapshot_ui` captures the editor, a sheet, Settings, Welcome or the recorder panel, with a
layout dump. `perform_menu_item` runs a menu item by path to put a sheet or
Settings up, `cancel_sheet` closes the sheet, and `select_inspector_tab`
picks an inspector tab and sub-tab. All four work with the
app inactive and its window covered. A capture's look is set at launch with
the dev-only `-RCDevAppearance light|dark`, never switched live. To see every
catalogued screen at once, `python3 tools/proof/screens.py` walks
`designs/screens/`, once per look, each time on its own pinned instance. It
writes each screen's PNGs and layout dumps and one `screens.md` with the
prose and each capture's layout problems. The last screen is the recorder
panel: shown from the background it no longer takes key (#137), but an
instance that is active when it runs still gets a key panel with Record on
Return, so the script stops each instance straight after capturing it.

Two rules from it worth carrying into any proof: **identical, stable,
DIFFERENT output across processes is an Auto Layout ambiguity to find, not a
race to out-wait** — reach for constraint priorities, not for more run-loop
turns (on an `NSStackView` that is `setHuggingPriority(_:for:)`;
`setContentHuggingPriority` is inert on a stack); and **when the thing to
check is app ARITHMETIC or app STRUCTURE with
no caller a script can reach** (a menu, a validator, a cue builder, a queue),
the answer is a probe compiled from `app/Sources` through
`tools/proof/swift_build.py`, not a photograph. A probe that will not build is a scored
FAILURE, never an exit, so a rotted instrument cannot take a score down with
it. **That rule applies to historical instruments too.** The meter and welcome
comparisons build old `app/Sources` with the matching old core and header in
isolated output directories, using the current guarded `harness/main.swift`
for both paints; `cloud_captions_probe.py`'s W and SP baselines build the
same way through `reference_build.py`, each in its own folder. A failed current or reference build is a scored failure,
including an FFI diagnostic; it is never a historical skip or a reason to
fall back to the old harness. Only the recording proof's granted tier can
skip rows for a named host condition such as a locked console.

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

# MCP Server Instructions

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## blender
You have access to Blender tools to interact with a Blender scene directly.
Blender must be running with the MCP add-on enabled and connected.

IMPORTANT: Respect existing structure and naming conventions.
NEVER assume missing values - inspect the scene first.
Do not destructively modify objects without confirmation.

# Bundled Manuals

Reference documentation is bundled alongside this server as plain-text RST files.
Search and read them directly with standard text tools (grep, file read, etc.):
  * `data/api/` - Blender Python API reference (RST files per module/class).
    Consult when writing or debugging `bpy` code: operator signatures, type
    properties, enum values, etc.
  * `data/manual/` - Blender user manual (RST files mirroring the official manual structure).
    Consult for conceptual explanations, workflow guidance, and feature overviews.

# Executing Code

The `execute_blender_code` tool runs Python code via `bpy` in the connected Blender instance.

The `execute_blender_code` tool is a last resort, if there are other tools that provide
the functionality you need, use those instead.

Prefer operators (`bpy.ops`) for standard actions (adding primitives, applying modifiers,
setting origins) - they handle defaults and context. Use the data API (`bpy.data`) for
precise control or to avoid side effects.

Many operators depend on the current mode (Object, Edit, Sculpt, etc.) and which objects
are active/selected. Verify or set the mode first - wrong mode either fails or silently
does nothing.

The **active object** and **selection** are distinct. Many operators require both.
Set them explicitly - do not assume the current state. Operators change selection and
active state as a side effect, so re-set both between sequential operator calls on
different objects.

Update the dependency graph after changes before reading computed properties
(world matrices, modifier results, etc.).

In edit mode, access mesh geometry through the bmesh API, not the regular mesh data API.
Flush bmesh changes back to the mesh - forgetting this silently loses all edits.

Return structured data (dicts, lists) from executed code, not print output.

# Scene & Data Structure

Blender uses a datablock system - objects and their underlying data (meshes, materials,
cameras, etc.) are separate entities.

Hierarchy:
  * **Scene** - top-level container. A .blend can have multiple.
  * **View Layer** - controls collection visibility/selectability.
  * **Collection** - organizational tree. Objects live in collections; can be nested;
    objects can belong to multiple collections.
  * **Object** - has a transform (location, rotation, scale) and references underlying data
    (Mesh, Curve, Camera, etc.). Multiple objects can share the same data (linked duplicates).
  * **Datablocks** - the actual data: geometry, materials, textures, etc.

Key concepts:
  * Objects and data are separate - deleting one does not delete the other.
  * Orphaned datablocks (zero users) are purged on save/reload or manual purge.
  * Objects created via the data API must be linked to a collection to appear in a scene.
  * Shared data: check user count before modifying a datablock - editing a shared mesh
    affects all objects referencing it. Make single-user first if needed.
  * In most cases file assets:
    * Images, Fonts, Sounds, other `.blend` files -  corraspond to a data-block.

Visibility has three independent states:
  * **Viewport hidden** - still fully scriptable.
  * **Disabled in view layer** - excluded; may be inaccessible to view-layer-dependent operators.
  * **Disabled for render** - skipped during render, otherwise normal.
Check these when objects seem "missing" or operators skip them.

Blender defaults to meters. Check scene unit settings before creating dimensioned objects.

Exploring scenes:
  * Walk the collection hierarchy for an overview first.
  * Don't dump entire scenes - inspect progressively for large scenes.
  * Check object types, parenting, modifiers, and materials before making changes.

The sentence = the item's text minus the comment, lines joined by one space; non-empty; Markdown kept. - Tutorial keys: `id` (required, `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*(\.[a-z][a-z0-9_]*)+$`, unique across the guide), `needs` (optional) `{"clip": <filter>}`. - Clip filter: optional `has_sound` bool, `has_pixels` bool, `kind` ∈ `media still image text shape graphic nest adjustment`, `follows_clip` bool (starts at or before the end of the previous clip on its track), `has_transition` bool (`transition_in` non-null). `{}` = any clip. - Step keys (all optional): `reveal`, `spotlight`, `wait`, `show_me`, `optional` (`true`: Skip offered, not required). - `reveal`: `{"tab": clip|media|document|assistant, "sub_tab"?: <ClipSubTab raw>, "section"?: <id>}`; `sub_tab` only with `tab` clip; `section` must be in the table and its home equal (`tab`, `sub_tab`). - `spotlight`: one string — a fixed name, `section:<id>` (id in the table), `clip:$selection` or `clip:$created`. - `wait` (≥1 condition, all must hold): `selection` `{min? int≥0 (default 1), max? int≥min, …filter keys}` (every selected clip matches); `changed` path or [paths] (a dotted clip-JSON path; met when any clip selected at step start differs there from step start); `clips` `{added: int≥1, kind?}`; `playhead` `{inside: "$selection"|"$created"}`; `range` exactly one of `{set: true}` / `{changed: "start"|"end"}`; `sheet` `"export"`; `export_started` `true` (the sheet's Export…, Add to Queue, or the `export` tool); `playing` `true`. No `wait` = Next. - `show_me`: `{"tool": <name>, "args"?: {…}}` | `{"menu": "<A ▸ B[ ▸ C]>"}` | a non-empty list of those, run in order. Tool: in the catalog, not in `dev_tools`; every args key in its `inputSchema.properties`; a literal string where the property has `enum` must be a member; for `set_video|set_audio|set_text|set_shape`, every leaf of `args.patch` as `<group>.<path>` must resolve in the fixture clips. Menu: an item path of the built menu bar whose leaf selector is a key of `inventory.json`'s `selectors`. - Variables (inside `show_me` args only, any depth): `"$selection"` → ids at step start; `"$created"` → ids added by the latest earlier step, or earlier call of this Show Me, that added any; `"$playhead"` → tick; `{"$pick": <filter>}` → id of the first matching clip in time order (ties: front track first); `{"$first": "$selection"|"$created"}` → earliest id; `{"$time": {"of": <ref>, "at": start|middle|end}}` → tick on the ref's span; `{"$track": "front"}` → the front track's id, resolved per call (so after an earlier `add_track` call of the same list it is that new, empty track). `<ref>` = `"$selection"`, `"$created"`, a `$pick` or a `$first`. Any other `$`-string or `$`-key is refused. - Sentence menu paths: `▸` only inside a bold span `**A ▸ B[ ▸ C]**`, which must be a leaf or submenu path of the built menu bar whose leaf selector is in `inventory.json`. **§B `Tutorials.json`** (`json.dumps(indent=1, ensure_ascii=False)`, pages sorted by file name, only pages with tutorials): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page": "audio.md", "title": "<the page's H1>", "tutorials": [{"id", "title", "anchor" (GitHub slug of the heading), "needs" (default {}), "steps": [{"text", …the step's machine-half keys verbatim}]}]}]}` **§C Swift** (`TutorialTargets.swift`): ```swift struct TutorialSectionHome: Equatable { let tab: InspectorTab; let subTab: ClipSubTab? } enum TutorialTargets { static let sectionPrefix = "section:" static let clipPrefix = "clip:" static let clipRefs: [String] // ["$selection", "$created"] static let fixed: [String: String] // name → the control, one line each static let sections: [String: TutorialSectionHome] // every InspectorSection id literal in app/Sources static func manifest() -> [String: Any] // {"fixed":[sorted],"sections":{id:{"tab","sub_tab"|null}},"clip_refs","tabs","sub_tabs"} } ``` Fixed names: `timeline.clips`, `ruler`, `canvas`, `toolbar.play`, `toolbar.timecode`, `toolbar.export`, `timeline.bar.{split,trim_start,trim_end,ripple_delete,add_marker,duplicate,add_text,add_shape}`, `inspector.tab.<InspectorTab title lowercased>` and `inspector.sub_tab.<ClipSubTab raw>` (built from `allCases`), `sheet.export.{format,size,frame_rate,quality,loudness,range,export,add_to_queue,cancel}`. Homes come from `ClipPane.makeSections()` (sound/text/shape/graphic/picture/color/clip), `DocumentPane` (`document`, nil), `MediaPane` (`media`, nil); `video.shadow` → picture. **§D Probe answer**: `ANSWER {"tools": {name: {"properties": {…}}}, "dev_tools": [AgentServer.devToolNames sorted], "targets": TutorialTargets.manifest(), "menu": [{"path": [titles], "selector": str|null, "submenu": bool}], "clips": [<the fixture project's clips array as the core writes it>]}`. --- a/CONTEXT.md
+++ b/CONTEXT.md
@@ -67,3 +67,11 @@ _Avoid_: backup, snapshot, undo step (restoring one is a file write, not undo),
 **Props**:
 The values a **Graphic** is drawn with, stored on its clip in the caller's key order — a title, an accent colour, a size. When the op that sets them carries the module's schema, each is checked by its dotted path (`props.accent`) for its type, its range and its options, and a colour is stored as lowercase hex; without one, only its shape. Distinct from a **Patch**, which is what a caller SENDS to change them: a patch's `props` merges into the stored props key by key, and a null in it removes that key (spec §11 G-4, G-12).
 _Avoid_: parameters, inputs, settings, variables
+
+**Tutorial**:
+A feature's steps, written once in its guide page as a numbered list under a `### Tutorial:` heading. A person can read them there, or the app can run them against the open project or the **Practice project**: each step's sentence is what the person reads, in the guide and in the app alike, and its machine half — an HTML comment the guide hides — says what the app opens first, what it points at, what counts as done and what Show Me does. It is the word in the menu (Help ▸ Tutorials) and in the code (spec §11 TU-1, TU-2).
+_Avoid_: walkthrough, wizard (which suggests the app makes the choices), lesson
+
+**Practice project**:
+A small project bundled with the app, with media made for the tutorials, in which every tutorial's needs are met. Help ▸ Tutorials opens it as an untitled copy, so the bundled one is never written; a **Tutorial** whose needs the open project does not meet offers it (spec §11 TU-5, TU-6).
+_Avoid_: sample project, demo, example project

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The guide's tutorials as one document (spec §11 TU-1, TU-2 (1)).
3	
4	    python3 tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py --guide docs/guide --out PATH/Tutorials.json
5	
6	A tutorial is a numbered list under a `### Tutorial: <title>` heading in a page
7	of `docs/guide/`, named by the `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under the
8	heading, each item's machine half an `<!-- step {json} -->` comment at its end.
9	This file is the ONE parser: the app build's "Write Tutorials" step runs it to
10	put `Tutorials.json` in the bundle, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` imports
11	`parse_guide` and checks the vocabulary on what it answers. Here only the
12	STRUCTURE is checked (TU-2 (1), the JSON, an `id` string, ids unique across
13	the guide); a page that breaks it is a `Problem` naming the page and the line,
14	printed `<page>:<line>: <message>`, and the exit is 1 with nothing written.
15	
16	The document (TU-1): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title", "tutorials":
17	[{"id", "title", "anchor", "needs", "steps": [{"text", …}]}]}]}`, pages sorted
18	by file name, only pages with a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1,
19	ensure_ascii=False)`. Stdlib only.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations  # the build step's PATH finds /usr/bin's Python 3.9 first
23	
24	import argparse
25	import json
26	import re
27	import sys
28	from pathlib import Path
29	from typing import NamedTuple
30	
31	FORMAT = 1
32	HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")
33	TUTORIAL_HEADING = re.compile(r"^###\s+Tutorial:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
34	ITEM = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)$")
35	FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
36	TUTORIAL_OPEN = "<!-- tutorial"
37	STEP_OPEN = "<!-- step"
38	CLOSE = "-->"
39	
40	
41	class Problem(NamedTuple):
42	    page: str
43	    line: int
44	    tutorial: str | None
45	    step: int | None
46	    message: str
47	
48	
49	def slug(text: str) -> str:
50	    """GitHub's heading anchor, without the duplicate suffix: lowercased, every
51	    character but a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore dropped, spaces
52	    made hyphens."""
53	    kept = "".join(ch for ch in text.lower() if ch.isalnum() or ch in " -_")
54	    return kept.replace(" ", "-")
55	
56	
57	def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
58	    """A heading's text as GitHub slugs it: links reduced to their words, code
59	    and emphasis marks dropped."""
60	    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
61	    return re.sub(r"[`*]", "", text)
62	
63	
64	def _comment(lines: list[str], start: int, opener: str):
65	    """The comment opening on `lines[start]` (which starts with `opener` after
66	    its indent) up to its `-->`: (json text, index of the closing line, the
67	    text after `-->`), or None when it never closes."""
68	    first = lines[start].split(opener, 1)[1]
69	    parts, index = [first], start
70	    while CLOSE not in parts[-1]:
71	        index += 1
72	        if index >= len(lines):
73	            return None
74	        parts.append(lines[index])
75	    joined = "\n".join(parts)
76	    body, after = joined.split(CLOSE, 1)
77	    return body.strip(), index, after.strip()
78	
79	
80	def _parse_json(text: str):
81	    try:
82	        return json.loads(text), None
83	    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
84	        return None, f"{error.msg} at column {error.colno}"
85	
86	
87	def _items(lines: list[str], start: int):
88	    """The ordered list starting at `lines[start]`: ([(number, first line index,
89	    [raw lines])], index after the list)."""
90	    items, index = [], start
91	    while index < len(lines):
92	        line = lines[index]
93	        match = ITEM.match(line)
94	        if match:
95	            items.append((int(match[1]), index, [match[2]]))
96	            index += 1
97	            continue
98	        if line.strip() == "":
99	            ahead = index + 1
100	            while ahead < len(lines) and lines[ahead].strip() == "":
101	                ahead += 1
102	            if ahead < len(lines) and items and (ITEM.match(lines[ahead])
103	                                                 or lines[ahead].startswith("   ")):
104	                index = ahead
105	                continue
106	            break
107	        if items and line.startswith("   "):
108	            items[-1][2].append(line)
109	            index += 1
110	            continue
111	        break
112	    return items, index
113	
114	
115	def _step(name, tutorial_id, number, first, raw, problems):
116	    """One item's step: {"text", …machine half}, or None after a Problem."""
117	    def fail(message, line=first):
118	        problems.append(Problem(name, line + 1, tutorial_id, number, message))
119	
120	    joined = "\n".join(raw)
121	    if joined.count(STEP_OPEN) > 1:
122	        fail("an item holds more than one `<!-- step` comment")
123	        return None
124	    half = {}
125	    text = joined
126	    if STEP_OPEN in joined:
127	        before, rest = joined.split(STEP_OPEN, 1)
128	        if CLOSE not in rest:
129	            fail("its `<!-- step` comment never closes")
130	            return None
131	        body, after = rest.split(CLOSE, 1)
132	        if after.strip():
133	            fail(f"text follows the step comment's `-->`: {after.strip()[:60]!r}")
134	            return None
135	        half, error = _parse_json(body.strip())
136	        if error:
137	            fail(f"its step JSON does not parse: {error}")
138	            return None
139	        if not isinstance(half, dict):
140	            fail("its step JSON is not an object")
141	            return None
142	        if "text" in half:
143	            fail("its step JSON has a `text` key, which is the sentence's")
144	            return None
145	        text = before
146	    sentence = " ".join(part.strip() for part in text.split("\n") if part.strip())
147	    if not sentence:
148	        fail("its sentence is empty")
149	        return None
150	    return {"text": sentence, **half}
151	
152	
153	def parse_page(name: str, text: str):
154	    """(page dict, or None when the page holds no tutorial, [Problem])."""
155	    lines = text.split("\n")
156	    problems: list[Problem] = []
157	    title, tutorials, slugs = None, [], {}
158	    claimed: set[int] = set()  # lines inside a parsed tutorial's comments and list
159	    fenced = False
160	    index = 0
161	    while index < len(lines):
162	        line = lines[index]
163	        if FENCE.match(line):
164	            fenced = not fenced
165	            index += 1
166	            continue
167	        heading = None if fenced else HEADING.match(line)
168	        if not heading:
169	            index += 1
170	            continue
171	        words = _strip_markup(heading[2])
172	        base = slug(words)
173	        count = slugs.get(base, 0)
174	        slugs[base] = count + 1
175	        anchor = base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}"
176	        if len(heading[1]) == 1 and title is None:
177	            title = heading[2]
178	        match = TUTORIAL_HEADING.match(line)
179	        if not match:
180	            index += 1
181	            continue
182	        heading_line = index
183	        tutorial, index = _tutorial(name, lines, index, match[1], anchor, problems, claimed)
184	        if tutorial is not None:
185	            tutorials.append((heading_line, tutorial))
186	        index = max(index, heading_line + 1)
187	    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
188	        if number not in claimed and (TUTORIAL_OPEN in line or STEP_OPEN in line):
189	            problems.append(Problem(name, number + 1, None, None,
190	                                    "a tutorial or step comment outside a tutorial's "
191	                                    "heading line or list"))
192	    if not tutorials:
193	        return None, problems
194	    if title is None:
195	        problems.append(Problem(name, 1, None, None, "the page has no `# ` title"))
196	    return {"page": name, "title": title or "", "tutorials": [t for _, t in tutorials]}, problems
197	
198	
199	def _tutorial(name, lines, index, title, anchor, problems, claimed):
200	    """The tutorial whose heading is `lines[index]`: (dict or None, next index)."""
201	    heading = index
202	    index += 1
203	    while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() == "":
204	        index += 1
205	    if index >= len(lines) or not lines[index].lstrip().startswith(TUTORIAL_OPEN) \
206	            or lines[index] != lines[index].lstrip():
207	        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, None, None,
208	                                "the line after a `### Tutorial:` heading is not "
209	                                "`<!-- tutorial {json} -->`"))
210	        return None, index
211	    found = _comment(lines, index, TUTORIAL_OPEN)
212	    if found is None:
213	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
214	                                "the `<!-- tutorial` comment never closes"))
215	        return None, index + 1
216	    body, closing, after = found
217	    claimed.update(range(index, closing + 1))
218	    if after:
219	        problems.append(Problem(name, closing + 1, None, None,
220	                                f"text follows the tutorial comment's `-->`: {after[:60]!r}"))
221	        return None, closing + 1
222	    head, error = _parse_json(body)
223	    if error or not isinstance(head, dict):
224	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
225	                                f"the tutorial JSON does not parse: {error}" if error
226	                                else "the tutorial JSON is not an object"))
227	        return None, closing + 1
228	    tutorial_id = head.get("id")
229	    if not isinstance(tutorial_id, str):
230	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
231	                                "the tutorial JSON has no string `id`"))
232	        return None, closing + 1
233	    unknown = sorted(set(head) - {"id", "needs"})
234	    if unknown:
235	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, tutorial_id, None,
236	                                f"unknown tutorial key {unknown[0]!r} (TU-2 (2): id, needs)"))
237	        return None, closing + 1
238	    index = closing + 1
239	    while index < len(lines) and not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
240	        if HEADING.match(lines[index]) or STEP_OPEN in lines[index] \
241	                or TUTORIAL_OPEN in lines[index]:
242	            break
243	        index += 1
244	    if index >= len(lines) or not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
245	        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, tutorial_id, None,
246	                                "the tutorial has no ordered list before the next heading"))
247	        return None, index
248	    items, after_list = _items(lines, index)
249	    claimed.update(range(index, after_list))
250	    steps = []
251	    for position, (number, first, raw) in enumerate(items, start=1):
252	        if number != position:
253	            problems.append(Problem(name, first + 1, tutorial_id, position,
254	                                    f"the list is numbered {number} where {position} belongs"))
255	            continue
256	        step = _step(name, tutorial_id, position, first, raw, problems)
257	        if step is not None:
258	            steps.append(step)
259	    if len(steps) != len(items):
260	        return None, after_list
261	    return {"id": tutorial_id, "title": title, "anchor": anchor,
262	            "needs": head.get("needs", {}), "steps": steps}, after_list
263	
264	
265	def parse_guide(folder: Path):
266	    """The TU-1 document over every `*.md` of `folder`, and every Problem,
267	    a second use of an id included."""
268	    folder = Path(folder)
269	    problems: list[Problem] = []
270	    pages, seen = [], {}
271	    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
272	        page, found = parse_page(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
273	        problems += found
274	        if page is None:
275	            continue
276	        for tutorial in page["tutorials"]:
277	            first = seen.get(tutorial["id"])
278	            if first is not None:
279	                problems.append(Problem(path.name, 0, tutorial["id"], None,
280	                                        f"the id {tutorial['id']!r} is already {first}'s"))
281	            else:
282	                seen[tutorial["id"]] = path.name
283	        pages.append(page)
284	    return {"format": FORMAT, "pages": pages}, problems
285	
286	
287	def render(document: dict) -> str:
288	    return json.dumps(document, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
289	
290	
291	def main(argv=None) -> int:
292	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
293	    parser.add_argument("--guide", required=True, type=Path)
294	    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
295	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
296	    if not args.guide.is_dir():
297	        print(f"tutorial_extract: {args.guide} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
298	        return 1
299	    document, problems = parse_guide(args.guide)
300	    if problems:

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""The guide's tutorials as one document (spec §11 TU-1, TU-2 (1)).

    python3 tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py --guide docs/guide --out PATH/Tutorials.json

A tutorial is a numbered list under a `### Tutorial: <title>` heading in a page
of `docs/guide/`, named by the `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under the
heading, each item's machine half an `<!-- step {json} -->` comment at its end.
This file is the ONE parser: the app build's "Write Tutorials" step runs it to
put `Tutorials.json` in the bundle, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` imports
`parse_guide` and checks the vocabulary on what it answers. Here only the
STRUCTURE is checked (TU-2 (1), the JSON, an `id` string, ids unique across
the guide); a page that breaks it is a `Problem` naming the page and the line,
printed `<page>:<line>: <message>`, and the exit is 1 with nothing written.

The document (TU-1): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title", "tutorials":
[{"id", "title", "anchor", "needs", "steps": [{"text", …}]}]}]}`, pages sorted
by file name, only pages with a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1,
ensure_ascii=False)`. Stdlib only.
"""

from __future__ import annotations  # the build step's PATH finds /usr/bin's Python 3.9 first

import argparse
import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from typing import NamedTuple

FORMAT = 1
HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")
TUTORIAL_HEADING = re.compile(r"^###\s+Tutorial:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
ITEM = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)$")
FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
TUTORIAL_OPEN = "<!-- tutorial"
STEP_OPEN = "<!-- step"
CLOSE = "-->"


class Problem(NamedTuple):
    page: str
    line: int
    tutorial: str | None
    step: int | None
    message: str


def slug(text: str) -> str:
    """GitHub's heading anchor, without the duplicate suffix: lowercased, every
    character but a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore dropped, spaces
    made hyphens."""
    kept = "".join(ch for ch in text.lower() if ch.isalnum() or ch in " -_")
    return kept.replace(" ", "-")


def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
    """A heading's text as GitHub slugs it: links reduced to their words, code
    and emphasis marks dropped."""
    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
    return re.sub(r"[`*]", "", text)


def _comment(lines: list[str], start: int, opener: str):
    """The comment opening on `lines[start]` (which starts with `opener` after
    its indent) up to its `-->`: (json text, index of the closing line, the
    text after `-->`), or None when it never closes."""
    first = lines[start].split(opener, 1)[1]
    parts, index = [first], start
    while CLOSE not in parts[-1]:
        index += 1
        if index >= len(lines):
            return None
        parts.append(lines[index])
    joined = "\n".join(parts)
    body, after = joined.split(CLOSE, 1)
    return body.strip(), index, after.strip()


def _parse_json(text: str):
    try:
        return json.loads(text), None
    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
        return None, f"{error.msg} at column {error.colno}"


def _items(lines: list[str], start: int):
    """The ordered list starting at `lines[start]`: ([(number, first line index,
    [raw lines])], index after the list)."""
    items, index = [], start
    while index < len(lines):
        line = lines[index]
        match = ITEM.match(line)
        if match:
            items.append((int(match[1]), index, [match[2]]))
            index += 1
            continue
        if line.strip() == "":
            ahead = index + 1
            while ahead < len(lines) and lines[ahead].strip() == "":
                ahead += 1
            if ahead < len(lines) and items and (ITEM.match(lines[ahead])
                                                 or lines[ahead].startswith("   ")):
                index = ahead
                continue
            break
        if items and line.startswith("   "):
            items[-1][2].append(line)
            index += 1
            continue
        break
    return items, index


def _step(name, tutorial_id, number, first, raw, problems):
    """One item's step: {"text", …machine half}, or None after a Problem."""
    def fail(message, line=first):
        problems.append(Problem(name, line + 1, tutorial_id, number, message))

    joined = "\n".join(raw)
    if joined.count(STEP_OPEN) > 1:
        fail("an item holds more than one `<!-- step` comment")
        return None
    half = {}
    text = joined
    if STEP_OPEN in joined:
        before, rest = joined.split(STEP_OPEN, 1)
        if CLOSE not in rest:
            fail("its `<!-- step` comment never closes")
            return None
        body, after = rest.split(CLOSE, 1)
        if after.strip():
            fail(f"text follows the step comment's `-->`: {after.strip()[:60]!r}")
            return None
        half, error = _parse_json(body.strip())
        if error:
            fail(f"its step JSON does not parse: {error}")
            return None
        if not isinstance(half, dict):
            fail("its step JSON is not an object")
            return None
        if "text" in half:
            fail("its step JSON has a `text` key, which is the sentence's")
            return None
        text = before
    sentence = " ".join(part.strip() for part in text.split("\n") if part.strip())
    if not sentence:
        fail("its sentence is empty")
        return None
    return {"text": sentence, **half}


def parse_page(name: str, text: str):
    """(page dict, or None when the page holds no tutorial, [Problem])."""
    lines = text.split("\n")
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    title, tutorials, slugs = None, [], {}
    claimed: set[int] = set()  # lines inside a parsed tutorial's comments and list
    fenced = False
    index = 0
    while index < len(lines):
        line = lines[index]
        if FENCE.match(line):
            fenced = not fenced
            index += 1
            continue
        heading = None if fenced else HEADING.match(line)
        if not heading:
            index += 1
            continue
        words = _strip_markup(heading[2])
        base = slug(words)
        count = slugs.get(base, 0)
        slugs[base] = count + 1
        anchor = base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}"
        if len(heading[1]) == 1 and title is None:
            title = heading[2]
        match = TUTORIAL_HEADING.match(line)
        if not match:
            index += 1
            continue
        heading_line = index
        tutorial, index = _tutorial(name, lines, index, match[1], anchor, problems, claimed)
        if tutorial is not None:
            tutorials.append((heading_line, tutorial))
        index = max(index, heading_line + 1)
    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
        if number not in claimed and (TUTORIAL_OPEN in line or STEP_OPEN in line):
            problems.append(Problem(name, number + 1, None, None,
                                    "a tutorial or step comment outside a tutorial's "
                                    "heading line or list"))
    if not tutorials:
        return None, problems
    if title is None:
        problems.append(Problem(name, 1, None, None, "the page has no `# ` title"))
    return {"page": name, "title": title or "", "tutorials": [t for _, t in tutorials]}, problems


def _tutorial(name, lines, index, title, anchor, problems, claimed):
    """The tutorial whose heading is `lines[index]`: (dict or None, next index)."""
    heading = index
    index += 1
    while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() == "":
        index += 1
    if index >= len(lines) or not lines[index].lstrip().startswith(TUTORIAL_OPEN) \
            or lines[index] != lines[index].lstrip():
        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, None, None,
                                "the line after a `### Tutorial:` heading is not "
                                "`<!-- tutorial {json} -->`"))
        return None, index
    found = _comment(lines, index, TUTORIAL_OPEN)
    if found is None:
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                "the `<!-- tutorial` comment never closes"))
        return None, index + 1
    body, closing, after = found
    claimed.update(range(index, closing + 1))
    if after:
        problems.append(Problem(name, closing + 1, None, None,
                                f"text follows the tutorial comment's `-->`: {after[:60]!r}"))
        return None, closing + 1
    head, error = _parse_json(body)
    if error or not isinstance(head, dict):
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                f"the tutorial JSON does not parse: {error}" if error
                                else "the tutorial JSON is not an object"))
        return None, closing + 1
    tutorial_id = head.get("id")
    if not isinstance(tutorial_id, str):
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
                                "the tutorial JSON has no string `id`"))
        return None, closing + 1
    unknown = sorted(set(head) - {"id", "needs"})
    if unknown:
        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, tutorial_id, None,
                                f"unknown tutorial key {unknown[0]!r} (TU-2 (2): id, needs)"))
        return None, closing + 1
    index = closing + 1
    while index < len(lines) and not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
        if HEADING.match(lines[index]) or STEP_OPEN in lines[index] \
                or TUTORIAL_OPEN in lines[index]:
            break
        index += 1
    if index >= len(lines) or not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, tutorial_id, None,
                                "the tutorial has no ordered list before the next heading"))
        return None, index
    items, after_list = _items(lines, index)
    claimed.update(range(index, after_list))
    steps = []
    for position, (number, first, raw) in enumerate(items, start=1):
        if number != position:
            problems.append(Problem(name, first + 1, tutorial_id, position,
                                    f"the list is numbered {number} where {position} belongs"))
            continue
        step = _step(name, tutorial_id, position, first, raw, problems)
        if step is not None:
            steps.append(step)
    if len(steps) != len(items):
        return None, after_list
    return {"id": tutorial_id, "title": title, "anchor": anchor,
            "needs": head.get("needs", {}), "steps": steps}, after_list


def parse_guide(folder: Path):
    """The TU-1 document over every `*.md` of `folder`, and every Problem,
    a second use of an id included."""
    folder = Path(folder)
    problems: list[Problem] = []
    pages, seen = [], {}
    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
        page, found = parse_page(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        problems += found
        if page is None:
            continue
        for tutorial in page["tutorials"]:
            first = seen.get(tutorial["id"])
            if first is not None:
                problems.append(Problem(path.name, 0, tutorial["id"], None,
                                        f"the id {tutorial['id']!r} is already {first}'s"))
            else:
                seen[tutorial["id"]] = path.name
        pages.append(page)
    return {"format": FORMAT, "pages": pages}, problems


def render(document: dict) -> str:
    return json.dumps(document, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"


def main(argv=None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--guide", required=True, type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if not args.guide.is_dir():
        print(f"tutorial_extract: {args.guide} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    document, problems = parse_guide(args.guide)
    if problems:
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"{problem.page}:{problem.line}: {problem.message}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 1
    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    text = render(document)
    if not args.out.exists() or args.out.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text:
        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
    count = sum(len(page["tutorials"]) for page in document["pages"])
    print(f"tutorial_extract: {count} tutorials in {len(document['pages'])} pages → {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""The guide's tutorials as one document (spec §11 TU-1, TU-2 (1)).
3	
4	    python3 tools/tutorials/tutorial_extract.py --guide docs/guide --out PATH/Tutorials.json
5	
6	A tutorial is a numbered list under a `### Tutorial: <title>` heading in a page
7	of `docs/guide/`, named by the `<!-- tutorial {json} -->` line under the
8	heading, each item's machine half an `<!-- step {json} -->` comment at its end.
9	This file is the ONE parser: the app build's "Write Tutorials" step runs it to
10	put `Tutorials.json` in the bundle, and `tools/proof/tutorial_check.py` imports
11	`parse_guide` and checks the vocabulary on what it answers. Here only the
12	STRUCTURE is checked (TU-2 (1), the JSON, an `id` string, ids unique across
13	the guide); a page that breaks it is a `Problem` naming the page and the line,
14	printed `<page>:<line>: <message>`, and the exit is 1 with nothing written.
15	
16	The document (TU-1): `{"format": 1, "pages": [{"page", "title", "tutorials":
17	[{"id", "title", "anchor", "needs", "steps": [{"text", …}]}]}]}`, pages sorted
18	by file name, only pages with a tutorial, `json.dumps(indent=1,
19	ensure_ascii=False)`. Stdlib only.
20	"""
21	
22	from __future__ import annotations  # the build step's PATH finds /usr/bin's Python 3.9 first
23	
24	import argparse
25	import json
26	import re
27	import sys
28	from pathlib import Path
29	from typing import NamedTuple
30	
31	FORMAT = 1
32	HEADING = re.compile(r"^(#{1,6})\s+(.*?)\s*#*\s*$")
33	TUTORIAL_HEADING = re.compile(r"^###\s+Tutorial:\s*(.*?)\s*$")
34	ITEM = re.compile(r"^(\d+)\.\s+(.*)$")
35	FENCE = re.compile(r"^\s*(```|~~~)")
36	TUTORIAL_OPEN = "<!-- tutorial"
37	STEP_OPEN = "<!-- step"
38	CLOSE = "-->"
39	
40	
41	class Problem(NamedTuple):
42	    page: str
43	    line: int
44	    tutorial: str | None
45	    step: int | None
46	    message: str
47	
48	
49	def slug(text: str) -> str:
50	    """GitHub's heading anchor, without the duplicate suffix: lowercased, every
51	    character but a letter, digit, space, hyphen or underscore dropped, spaces
52	    made hyphens."""
53	    kept = "".join(ch for ch in text.lower() if ch.isalnum() or ch in " -_")
54	    return kept.replace(" ", "-")
55	
56	
57	def _strip_markup(text: str) -> str:
58	    """A heading's text as GitHub slugs it: links reduced to their words, code
59	    and emphasis marks dropped."""
60	    text = re.sub(r"\[([^\]]*)\]\([^)]*\)", r"\1", text)
61	    return re.sub(r"[`*]", "", text)
62	
63	
64	def _comment(lines: list[str], start: int, opener: str):
65	    """The comment opening on `lines[start]` (which starts with `opener` after
66	    its indent) up to its `-->`: (json text, index of the closing line, the
67	    text after `-->`), or None when it never closes."""
68	    first = lines[start].split(opener, 1)[1]
69	    parts, index = [first], start
70	    while CLOSE not in parts[-1]:
71	        index += 1
72	        if index >= len(lines):
73	            return None
74	        parts.append(lines[index])
75	    joined = "\n".join(parts)
76	    body, after = joined.split(CLOSE, 1)
77	    return body.strip(), index, after.strip()
78	
79	
80	def _parse_json(text: str):
81	    try:
82	        return json.loads(text), None
83	    except json.JSONDecodeError as error:
84	        return None, f"{error.msg} at column {error.colno}"
85	
86	
87	def _items(lines: list[str], start: int):
88	    """The ordered list starting at `lines[start]`: ([(number, first line index,
89	    [raw lines])], index after the list)."""
90	    items, index = [], start
91	    while index < len(lines):
92	        line = lines[index]
93	        match = ITEM.match(line)
94	        if match:
95	            items.append((int(match[1]), index, [match[2]]))
96	            index += 1
97	            continue
98	        if line.strip() == "":
99	            ahead = index + 1
100	            while ahead < len(lines) and lines[ahead].strip() == "":
101	                ahead += 1
102	            if ahead < len(lines) and items and (ITEM.match(lines[ahead])
103	                                                 or lines[ahead].startswith("   ")):
104	                index = ahead
105	                continue
106	            break
107	        if items and line.startswith("   "):
108	            items[-1][2].append(line)
109	            index += 1
110	            continue
111	        break
112	    return items, index
113	
114	
115	def _step(name, tutorial_id, number, first, raw, problems):
116	    """One item's step: {"text", …machine half}, or None after a Problem."""
117	    def fail(message, line=first):
118	        problems.append(Problem(name, line + 1, tutorial_id, number, message))
119	
120	    joined = "\n".join(raw)
121	    if joined.count(STEP_OPEN) > 1:
122	        fail("an item holds more than one `<!-- step` comment")
123	        return None
124	    half = {}
125	    text = joined
126	    if STEP_OPEN in joined:
127	        before, rest = joined.split(STEP_OPEN, 1)
128	        if CLOSE not in rest:
129	            fail("its `<!-- step` comment never closes")
130	            return None
131	        body, after = rest.split(CLOSE, 1)
132	        if after.strip():
133	            fail(f"text follows the step comment's `-->`: {after.strip()[:60]!r}")
134	            return None
135	        half, error = _parse_json(body.strip())
136	        if error:
137	            fail(f"its step JSON does not parse: {error}")
138	            return None
139	        if not isinstance(half, dict):
140	            fail("its step JSON is not an object")
141	            return None
142	        if "text" in half:
143	            fail("its step JSON has a `text` key, which is the sentence's")
144	            return None
145	        text = before
146	    sentence = " ".join(part.strip() for part in text.split("\n") if part.strip())
147	    if not sentence:
148	        fail("its sentence is empty")
149	        return None
150	    return {"text": sentence, **half}
151	
152	
153	def parse_page(name: str, text: str):
154	    """(page dict, or None when the page holds no tutorial, [Problem])."""
155	    lines = text.split("\n")
156	    problems: list[Problem] = []
157	    title, tutorials, slugs = None, [], {}
158	    claimed: set[int] = set()  # lines inside a parsed tutorial's comments and list
159	    fenced = False
160	    index = 0
161	    while index < len(lines):
162	        line = lines[index]
163	        if FENCE.match(line):
164	            fenced = not fenced
165	            index += 1
166	            continue
167	        heading = None if fenced else HEADING.match(line)
168	        if not heading:
169	            index += 1
170	            continue
171	        words = _strip_markup(heading[2])
172	        base = slug(words)
173	        count = slugs.get(base, 0)
174	        slugs[base] = count + 1
175	        anchor = base if count == 0 else f"{base}-{count}"
176	        if len(heading[1]) == 1 and title is None:
177	            title = heading[2]
178	        match = TUTORIAL_HEADING.match(line)
179	        if not match:
180	            index += 1
181	            continue
182	        heading_line = index
183	        tutorial, index = _tutorial(name, lines, index, match[1], anchor, problems, claimed)
184	        if tutorial is not None:
185	            tutorials.append((heading_line, tutorial))
186	        index = max(index, heading_line + 1)
187	    for number, line in enumerate(lines):
188	        if number not in claimed and (TUTORIAL_OPEN in line or STEP_OPEN in line):
189	            problems.append(Problem(name, number + 1, None, None,
190	                                    "a tutorial or step comment outside a tutorial's "
191	                                    "heading line or list"))
192	    if not tutorials:
193	        return None, problems
194	    if title is None:
195	        problems.append(Problem(name, 1, None, None, "the page has no `# ` title"))
196	    return {"page": name, "title": title or "", "tutorials": [t for _, t in tutorials]}, problems
197	
198	
199	def _tutorial(name, lines, index, title, anchor, problems, claimed):
200	    """The tutorial whose heading is `lines[index]`: (dict or None, next index)."""
201	    heading = index
202	    index += 1
203	    while index < len(lines) and lines[index].strip() == "":
204	        index += 1
205	    if index >= len(lines) or not lines[index].lstrip().startswith(TUTORIAL_OPEN) \
206	            or lines[index] != lines[index].lstrip():
207	        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, None, None,
208	                                "the line after a `### Tutorial:` heading is not "
209	                                "`<!-- tutorial {json} -->`"))
210	        return None, index
211	    found = _comment(lines, index, TUTORIAL_OPEN)
212	    if found is None:
213	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
214	                                "the `<!-- tutorial` comment never closes"))
215	        return None, index + 1
216	    body, closing, after = found
217	    claimed.update(range(index, closing + 1))
218	    if after:
219	        problems.append(Problem(name, closing + 1, None, None,
220	                                f"text follows the tutorial comment's `-->`: {after[:60]!r}"))
221	        return None, closing + 1
222	    head, error = _parse_json(body)
223	    if error or not isinstance(head, dict):
224	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
225	                                f"the tutorial JSON does not parse: {error}" if error
226	                                else "the tutorial JSON is not an object"))
227	        return None, closing + 1
228	    tutorial_id = head.get("id")
229	    if not isinstance(tutorial_id, str):
230	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, None, None,
231	                                "the tutorial JSON has no string `id`"))
232	        return None, closing + 1
233	    unknown = sorted(set(head) - {"id", "needs"})
234	    if unknown:
235	        problems.append(Problem(name, index + 1, tutorial_id, None,
236	                                f"unknown tutorial key {unknown[0]!r} (TU-2 (2): id, needs)"))
237	        return None, closing + 1
238	    index = closing + 1
239	    while index < len(lines) and not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
240	        if HEADING.match(lines[index]) or STEP_OPEN in lines[index] \
241	                or TUTORIAL_OPEN in lines[index]:
242	            break
243	        index += 1
244	    if index >= len(lines) or not ITEM.match(lines[index]):
245	        problems.append(Problem(name, heading + 1, tutorial_id, None,
246	                                "the tutorial has no ordered list before the next heading"))
247	        return None, index
248	    items, after_list = _items(lines, index)
249	    claimed.update(range(index, after_list))
250	    steps = []
251	    for position, (number, first, raw) in enumerate(items, start=1):
252	        if number != position:
253	            problems.append(Problem(name, first + 1, tutorial_id, position,
254	                                    f"the list is numbered {number} where {position} belongs"))
255	            continue
256	        step = _step(name, tutorial_id, position, first, raw, problems)
257	        if step is not None:
258	            steps.append(step)
259	    if len(steps) != len(items):
260	        return None, after_list
261	    return {"id": tutorial_id, "title": title, "anchor": anchor,
262	            "needs": head.get("needs", {}), "steps": steps}, after_list
263	
264	
265	def parse_guide(folder: Path):
266	    """The TU-1 document over every `*.md` of `folder`, and every Problem,
267	    a second use of an id included."""
268	    folder = Path(folder)
269	    problems: list[Problem] = []
270	    pages, seen = [], {}
271	    for path in sorted(folder.glob("*.md")):
272	        page, found = parse_page(path.name, path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
273	        problems += found
274	        if page is None:
275	            continue
276	        for tutorial in page["tutorials"]:
277	            first = seen.get(tutorial["id"])
278	            if first is not None:
279	                problems.append(Problem(path.name, 0, tutorial["id"], None,
280	                                        f"the id {tutorial['id']!r} is already {first}'s"))
281	            else:
282	                seen[tutorial["id"]] = path.name
283	        pages.append(page)
284	    return {"format": FORMAT, "pages": pages}, problems
285	
286	
287	def render(document: dict) -> str:
288	    return json.dumps(document, indent=1, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n"
289	
290	
291	def main(argv=None) -> int:
292	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
293	    parser.add_argument("--guide", required=True, type=Path)
294	    parser.add_argument("--out", required=True, type=Path)
295	    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
296	    if not args.guide.is_dir():
297	        print(f"tutorial_extract: {args.guide} is not a folder", file=sys.stderr)
298	        return 1
299	    document, problems = parse_guide(args.guide)
300	    if problems:
301	        for problem in problems:
302	            print(f"{problem.page}:{problem.line}: {problem.message}", file=sys.stderr)
303	        return 1
304	    args.out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
305	    text = render(document)
306	    if not args.out.exists() or args.out.read_text(encoding="utf-8") != text:
307	        args.out.write_text(text, encoding="utf-8")
308	    count = sum(len(page["tutorials"]) for page in document["pages"])
309	    print(f"tutorial_extract: {count} tutorials in {len(document['pages'])} pages → {args.out}")
310	    return 0
311	
312	
313	if __name__ == "__main__":
314	    sys.exit(main())
